Our player pathway at work

From our U16s and U18 Floodlit team to the Reserves and First Team football at Step 6, we're building a genuine pathway for young players at Eccleshall FC.

Yesterday, 16-year-old Gael became the latest U18 player to step up, with Charlie Padania progressing from the Reserves and U16 goalkeeper Juke Gibbs also gaining experience in the First Team environment.

They follow Will Silvester, Mikey Dempsey, Theo Pinto and Charlie Ashcroft in showing what we're trying to create.

We're also proud of our relationship with RTC, with Gael, Theo and Charlie all joining us through that connection.

💔🕊️ IN LOVING MEMORY OF JACK EVANS 🕊️💔

Forever a Dawley lad. Forever in our hearts. ❤️

This Saturday, Dawley Town Football Club will come together as one family to remember and pay our respects to Jack Evans, who tragically passed away last week.

Jack was a proud Dawley lad, a familiar face to so many in our community and a friend to many of our players, particularly Dan Beddows.

His passing has left a huge hole in the lives of those who knew and loved him, and our entire football club is deeply saddened by his loss.

But above all else, Jack was a dad.

A loving father to Scarlett, Jacob, Teddy and Sienna, four children who will forever carry their dad’s love and memory with them.

Our thoughts, prayers and deepest sympathies are with Jack’s children, their mothers Louise and Laura, his family, friends and everyone whose life he touched.

❤️ THIS SATURDAY – TOGETHER FOR JACK ❤️

As a mark of respect, Jack’s four children will have the honour of walking onto the pitch alongside our players before kick-off.

We ask everyone attending the game, players, officials and supporters alike, to join us in observing a minute’s silence in Jack’s memory.

There will also be a collection bucket at the entrance, with all donations going directly towards supporting Jack’s family during this incredibly difficult time.

Whatever you can spare, however big or small, will be greatly appreciated.

🖤 MEN’S MENTAL HEALTH – YOU ARE NEVER ALONE 🖤

Jack’s passing is a heartbreaking reminder of just how precious life is and how important it is that we look out for one another.

As a football club, we want to use this opportunity to encourage men everywhere to talk, to reach out and to know that asking for help is a sign of strength, never weakness.

Whether it’s a teammate, a friend, a family member or someone you haven’t spoken to in a while, sometimes the simplest conversation can make the biggest difference.

If you’re struggling, please reach out. There are people who care and people who will listen.

💚 SUPPORT IS AVAILABLE:

🦁 PRIMAL INSTINCTS – TELFORD
A local men’s mental health support community, helping men connect, talk openly and support one another.

📞 SAMARITANS: 116 123
Free, confidential support, 24 hours a day.

💙 CALM (Campaign Against Living Miserably): 0800 58 58 58
Suicide prevention and mental health support.

💚 MIND: 0300 123 3393
Mental health information, advice and support.

🖤 SHOUT: Text SHOUT to 85258
Free, confidential text support, 24/7.

💙 ANDY’S MAN CLUB
Free peer-to-peer support groups for men aged 18 and over.
It’s Okay To Talk.

If you or someone else is in immediate danger, call 999.

⚽ MORE THAN A FOOTBALL CLUB. WE ARE A COMMUNITY.

Football brings people together, but moments like this remind us that some things are far more important than the result on a Saturday afternoon.

This weekend isn’t about football.

It’s about Jack. It’s about his children. It’s about his family. And it’s about a community standing together when it matters most.

Rest easy, Jack. 🕊️

Once a Dawley lad, always a Dawley lad. ❤️

From everyone at Dawley Town Football Club.
